# Ethics-Relational @ Stage 9 — Primary / Modern

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 72 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Ethics-relational at Order 7 is **systematic relational design**: the deliberate
construction of ethical systems based on explicit principles. "I design this ethical
system because I have reasoned about it" — ethical design is self-authored rather than
inherited. The ethicist who constructs a systematic care ethics theory, the therapist
who designs a relational healing protocol, the leader who designs an ethically
supportive culture — these are Stage 9 relational architects.

The key advance from Stage 8 is **systemic relational modeling**. The agent does not
just see multiple perspectives on ethics — it sees how relational processes interact as
a dynamic system with feedback loops, emergent properties, and structural constraints.

Ethics at Stage 9 is understood as **designable**. The agent believes that relational
responsibility can be intentionally improved through rational analysis and systematic
design. This is the modernist ethics: relationships are engineering problems that can
be solved with the right design.

But relational reasoning at Stage 9 is still **framework-bound**. The agent designs
ethical systems within a particular framework (utilitarian, deontological, care ethics)
but cannot step outside the framework to evaluate it.

The transition from Stage 9 to Stage 10 occurs when the agent can evaluate entire
ethical frameworks.

In human development, Stage 9 corresponds to the professional who can construct and
defend a systematic ethical theory.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Institutional relational design culture emerges. Universities, ethics
  institutes, relational research centers.

- **UR:** The individual agent can construct and evaluate ethical systems using
  explicit principles.

- **LL:** Systemic ethical institutions emerge: ethical codes, relational research
  centers, care-based organizations.

- **LR:** The ethics institute, the relational research center, the care-based
  organization.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Methodological hubris — the belief that one's ethical approach
  is objectively true and all others are wrong.

- **Dark allergy:** Anti-ethical nihilism — the rejection of all systematic relational
  reasoning.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to systematic relational reasoning as the only valid
  approach.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting systematic ethics as dehumanizing.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Systemic relational modeling:** The agent can trace relational dynamics and
  predict how changes affect ethical outcomes.

- **Design-based relational reasoning:** The agent proposes relational improvements
  based on analysis.

- **Framework-bound analysis:** The agent reasons brilliantly within an ethical
  framework but cannot evaluate the framework itself.

- **Expert-dependent design:** Ethical design is concentrated in professionals.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Noddings, N. (1984). *Caring: A Feminine Approach to Ethics* — systematic care
  ethics
- Gilligan, C. (1982). *In a Different Voice* — systematic relational theory
- Rawls, J. (1971). *A Theory of Justice* — systematic justice theory
